standard_prerequisites.name: A disjoint union of finitely many affine schemes is affine, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the comparison morphism used in the reduction a morphism of affine schemes.

standard_prerequisites.name: The algebra criterion that a ring map has dense image exactly when the generic point of every irreducible component of the target lies in the image of the corresponding morphism of spectra
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the conclusion in the affine case, to which the proof reduces.

core_obligations: Reduce to a morphism of affine schemes: for an affine open of the target use quasi-compactness to cover its preimage by finitely many affine opens, form the morphism from their disjoint union (which is affine) to that affine open, and note that dominance of the original morphism is equivalent to dominance of this comparison morphism, while its generic points are exactly those of the components of the target meeting that affine open (proof lines 1282-1300).
Apply the affine criterion: for morphisms of affine schemes the statement is the cited algebra criterion about dense images and generic points, which finishes the proof (proof lines 1301-1302).
proof_roadmap: Cover the preimage of an affine open by finitely many affines and replace the morphism by an affine one without changing dominance or the relevant generic points (proof lines 1282-1300), then quote the affine case (proof lines 1301-1302).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a quasi-compact morphism is dominant exactly when the generic point of every irreducible component of the target lies in its image (statement lines 1271-1280). The counted proof is a short reduction to the affine case: quasi-compactness lets one cover the preimage of an affine open by finitely many affines, whose disjoint union is again affine, and dominance as well as the relevant generic points are unaffected by this replacement, after which the affine algebra criterion applies (proof lines 1282-1302). It is H2: the reduction is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the affineness of finite disjoint unions and the affine criterion.
